physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the sternum, the flat bone at the centre of the chest, the place the ribs come home to. It is the body's plumb line. Lay a hand there and you find the still point that does not move while breath moves around it, the quiet pole the body orients itself from without ever being told to.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. Dislocation is not only a feeling in the mind, it sits in the chest. The breath gets shallow and stays high. The shoulders creep forward. The sternum closes over the heart like a door pulled to, and the centre line goes vague. A person who has lost the thread carries it in the bones first. You can see it in the way they stand.

The climb out is also bodily, and it begins lower than thinking. The chest softens. The breath drops. The bone at the centre comes back into its place and the line through the body is found again, not by deciding to find it but by stopping the work of holding it shut. Orientation is not a direction chosen. It is the body remembering its own midline.

The code is seated in the bone that protects the heart, and it teaches at the same depth. To be oriented is to let the centre be the centre. Nothing else has to be done.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the bone, this code answers to a single amino acid, Phenylalanine. It belongs, like the amino acid of the first code, to the small group the body cannot make for itself. It must be taken in from outside, carried across the line of the mouth, broken down, put to use.

What the body does with it is the teaching. Phenylalanine is the raw material the body turns into the chemistry of signalling, the messengers that tell one part of the system where another part is, that keep the inside in conversation with itself. The substance of orientation is literally built from it. Without it, the body cannot hear itself thinking.

There is a quiet shock in that. The code of finding your way is laid down in a chemistry the body cannot manufacture. The thing you call homing, the inward pull back to the centre, runs on something that had to be received. You were never going to orient yourself by yourself. The world was always part of the recipe.
